finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Passing an attacker-controlled string to printf without proper validation
finding.assumptions: The main function calls is_balanced with strings that are not controlled by the attacker. However, if the input to is_balanced comes from an untrusted source, it could lead to command injection.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
Checked that the only printf calls in the fragment are: 
1. The debug prints in is_balanced (lines 26, 35, 52, 58) all use static format strings with no user input.
2. The main function prints the result of is_balanced using a fixed format "%d\n" (lines 67-71). The 'expression' argument never reaches a printf as a format string.
Thus there is no data path from the untrusted source to a printf sink that could lead to format string or command injection. The reported vulnerability is a false positive.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: Pushing more symbols onto the stack than its capacity (MAX_SIZE)
finding.assumptions: The input to is_balanced is not validated to ensure it does not exceed the stack's capacity. If the input is attacker-controlled, it could lead to a buffer overflow.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the push function: it calls is_full (line 25) which correctly guards against exceeding MAX_SIZE. The guard exits before the array write at line 29, preventing a buffer overflow. The pop function similarly guards against underflow before accessing the array at line 37.
